season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — that exact overcorrection sat live in your Week 4 lineup for five straight days (Shough over Herbert) until this run flagged it again.

Left the QB slot completely empty all week (Shough would've scored 15.94 sitting there unused) and started Josh Downs (4.6) over Omarion Hampton (13.3) in the flex — an 8.7-point unforced error stacked on a totally wasted roster slot. A win over a weak opponent papered over the worst bench-management week of the season so far; double-check every single slot is filled before Thursday lock, every week, no exceptions.

Nothing was mismanaged this week (Herbert/Tuten/Brown/Higgins/Wilson/Strange/Downs/Flowers/Aubrey/Jaguars was the right call going in) — Weak Homie Quon just had a bigger week. First game with Mike Gesicki rostered: he scored 7.4 on the bench in his debut, real TE depth for the first time all season. Separately, Jaguars DEF cratered to 2.0 for the second time in three weeks despite a plus matchup grade — stop trusting the defRank alone for that unit, check the actual opposing offense's health too.

Correctly sat Tee Higgins and Chase Brown through Cincinnati's bye (both would've scored 0 either way), but still left 10.9 points on the bench elsewhere: Dameon Pierce (15.0) outscored started RB Woody Marks (10.1) by 4.9, and bench K Jason Myers (7.0) beat started K Brandon Aubrey (1.0) by 6.0. Bigger trap now unfolding into Week 7: Bhayshul Tuten's huge Week 6 output (24.7) and a quiet Herbert bench week apparently prompted a swap into both of them as Week 7 starters — except Jacksonville AND the Chargers are both on bye Week 7. Don't chase last week's box score without checking the bye schedule first.

Bench K Brandon Aubrey (14.0) outscored started Jason Myers (8.0) by 6.0 — the week's only avoidable miss; Tuten and Hampton both being on bye forced the rest of the lineup, no mistake there. The bigger story heading into Week 8: Tyler Shough is your ONLY rostered QB, and New Orleans' bye lands this week — a zero-QB-depth problem that's been sitting unnoticed on this roster all season and is now live. Fix it on waivers, and keep a real backup QB rostered going forward so a single bye week doesn't cost you a start.
